summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis, vasculitis, and POTS was admitted for recurrent abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting consistent with a flare of her chronic pancreatitis. She initially presented with right upper quadrant pain that progressed to epigastric pain, associated with bilious emesis and an episode of blood-tinged vomitus. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, IV Dilaudid for pain, and Zofran for nausea. Her lipase was only mildly elevated, but clinical presentation supported a pancreatic flare. She gradually improved, tolerated advancement to a regular diet, and successfully transitioned to oral pain and nausea medications. Methotrexate was administered during admission. She was discharged home in stable condition with controlled pain, tolerating oral intake, and instructions to continue her medications, including pancreatic enzyme supplements and new stool softeners to prevent opioid-induced constipation.
